notes: Tier 1 (direct HTTP) sufficed; site is a standard Shopify storefront (robots.txt: 'User-agent: *  Allow: /', no Claude-specific disallow, explicit UCP/agents.md invitation for agentic crawling). Enumerated the FULL site taxonomy via /collections.json?limit=250 (54 collections total, confirmed complete since page=2/3 returned empty) and cross-checked against sitemap_collections_1.xml (same 54 URLs) and the homepage nav <a href> list (subset of same 54) -- three independent sources agree on the full collection roster. None of the 54 collection titles/handles name any holiday or festival: they are all product-type/series/brand groupings (Bowls, Dinner Sets, Coffee Mugs, Tea Sets, Plates, Platters, JCPL, India Circus, Wishing Chair, Disney, Sale, New Arrivals, price-tier collections, etc). Checked specifically for Diwali given the company profile (Indian ceramics/dinnerware, diyas/decorative items are core Diwali categories): no 'Diwali' collection exists. Found one collection titled 'Festive Gift Collection' (handle festive-collection, 20 products) whose on-page <title> and meta description are generic ('curated for users who are looking for great gifting choices in the festive season') -- fetched its full product list via /collections/festive-collection/products.json and found only 8 of 20 products have 'diwali-gift-set' in their product handle/name; the remaining 12 are ordinary 'premium collection' plates/bowls/tea-sets with no seasonal naming. Per the boundary rule that a category which merely contains some seasonal products (and whose own site-given name/label is generic, not holiday-specific) is not itself a seasonal category, this was excluded as MANUAL-REVIEW-considered-and-rejected, not included. Checked the homepage's embedded Instagram-highlights widget (useifsapp.com feed) which surfaces highlight reels titled 'Holi Hues' and 'RAKHI', and post captions referencing Raksha Bandhan -- these are social-media embeds, not PLP/category pages with their own URL and product grid, so they fail the genuine-PLP test and were excluded. Checked internal site search (/search?q=...) for diwali, christmas, rakhi, holi, new-year, valentine, easter, eid -- each returns a generic keyword-relevance product list (not a curated PLP/category, and per rules search results are not proof of presence or absence on their own); none surfaced any additional dedicated seasonal collection URL beyond what enumeration already found. Checked /pages sitemap (24 pages: about-us, policies, corporate-gifts, hotelware, warranty, blog, etc) -- no seasonal landing page. Also explicitly checked for Christmas, Halloween, New Year, Holi, Raksha Bandhan/Rakhi, Valentine's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, Eid, Mother's Day, Father's Day by name across collection titles/handles, nav links, and homepage text -- none present as a genuine PLP category. Conclusion: this ceramics/dinnerware/kitchenware retailer organizes its entire catalog by product type, material/finish series, and brand collaboration, not by festival/season; it has zero genuine seasonal/holiday PLP categories despite carrying individual Diwali-gift-set SKUs inside a generically-named gifting collection.
